messageValues.message: You assess reports of personal data breaches. Report a risk factor only when you can quote, word for word, the part of the BREACH DESCRIPTION that shows it. Never infer from silence, never repeat a factor that is already met, and never argue that a factor does not apply. Reply with JSON matching the requested schema and nothing else.

parameters.content:
## Assess a personal data breach against the GDPR 72 hour deadline

### How it works
Somebody reports a suspected breach on a form. A Set node holds the deadline and thresholds; ten risk factors live in a data table you can edit. A Code node scores the report deterministically: each Yes answer and each keyword in the description counts a factor, and the 72 hour clock runs from the moment you became aware, not from when the incident happened. A Groq call then reads the description and may add a factor only when it quotes the exact words that show it; a suggestion without a verbatim quote is discarded. Any high severity factor gives NOTIFY_AUTHORITY_AND_SUBJECTS, any other gives NOTIFY_AUTHORITY, none gives RECORD_ONLY, and an empty factor table, a description too short to read or an unreadable awareness date give INCOMPLETE, never a quiet pass. Every assessment goes to breach_register and every factor to breach_findings. Notifiable breaches go to Discord and the reporter is shown what to do next. A daily watchdog then chases notifiable breaches whose register row still says the authority was not told.

### Setup
1. Add a Groq credential to the Groq node and a Discord webhook to both Discord nodes.
2. Run Set Up Tables once. It creates four data tables and loads the ten risk factors; every other node finds its table by name.
3. Open the form and report a test breach with health data that is still exposed.
4. Set authority_notified to yes in breach_register once you have reported, or the watchdog keeps chasing.

### Customization tips
Edit the factors and their keywords in breach_risk_factors; the table is the policy. Keywords are English, so a report in another language matches fewer of them. This is a triage aid, not legal advice.

## 1. Create the tables and load the ten risk factors (run once)
Four tables are created with typed columns, or reused when the names already exist. The ten factors are upserted by key, so running this a second time changes nothing. [Data table node docs](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.datatable/)

## 2. Report and score
The [form](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.formtrigger/) collects the breach. Set Breach Policy holds the deadline and thresholds. Each Yes answer and each keyword hit counts a factor, and the deadline is measured from the awareness date.

## 3. Review and decide
The [LLM Chain](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.chainllm/) reviewer may add a factor only with a verbatim quote that is checked against the report text. It can raise the verdict and can never lower it.

## 4. Record
One row per assessment in breach_register with the deadline and the report, one row per factor in breach_findings with its evidence, or a none row so every assessment leaves a trace.

## 5. Escalate and answer
Notifiable breaches go to [Discord](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.discord/), then the reporter sees one of three pages: authority and people, authority only, or documented. Swap Discord for Slack or Gmail.

## 6. Daily deadline watchdog
The [Schedule Trigger](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.scheduletrigger/) reads the register, keeps the notifiable rows whose authority_notified is not yes, and reports the ones overdue or inside the warning window. Every run writes a row, including a quiet one.
